- Message: Learn the basics of schema design, data types, and optimization. Hi Anu, The inherent flexibility of MongoDB's document model makes the initial setup easy. However, the performance and scalability of your application depend significantly on how you structure your data. Start modeling <https://cloud.mongodb.com/go?l=https%3A%2F%2Fcloud.mongodb.com%2Fv2%23%2Forg%2F%3Corganization%3E%2Fprojects> Data modeling for high performance In MongoDB, you can model data in JSON the same way you do in code, as intuitive objects. Unlike in relational approaches, optimizing for performance in MongoDB follows a few simple guidelines. * When to embed data <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/concepts/embedding-vs-references/#embedded-data-models> : Data that is accessed together should be stored together. For "one-to-few" relationships (like a user and their shipping addresses), embedding the addresses inside the user document is ideal. This improves query performance and enables low-latency performance at scale. * Reference data with one-to-many relationships <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/model-referenced-one-to-many-relationships-between-documents/> : For "one-to-many

Query Insights gives you a clear, cluster-wide view of which queries are impacting performance. Launch Query Insights <https://cloud.mongodb.com/v2/64f0d460ce4e047320892068#/metrics/replicaSet/6973fb74c881ef3df8b66e0b/queryInsights/profiler?fromCta=queryInsightsPage&metric=Operation+Execution+Time&since=1775061477206&until=1775147877206> With Query Insights, you can: * Identify queries with high execution times across your clusters and collections * Understand the impact of queries before and after adding indexes * Isolate inefficient queries involving specific stages like lookup or sort * Track performance trends over time to validate improvements Check out this video for a deeper walkthrough on how to fix slow queries. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CmVoX2bOCEo> Looking to give your team access to Query Insights? Add Project Observability Viewer roleshere <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles/#mongodb-authrole-Project-Observability-Viewer> .
